---
title: Run it yourself
description: Clone it, point it at Postgres, and run the web app and the engine. Run your own keeper and you earn the 0.5% opener fee on every round you open.
icon: Server
---

<Steps>
<Step>

### Install

Node 24 and pnpm 12.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Blockchain-Oracle/joge && cd joge && pnpm install
```

</Step>
<Step>

### Configure

`services/engine/.env` and `apps/web/.env.local`:

| Variable | For |
|---|---|
| `DATABASE_URL` | Both: a Postgres 17 database (the engine migrates it on start) |
| `JOGE_NETWORK` | Engine: `chipnet` or `mainnet` |
| `KEEPER_WIF` | Engine: the key that pays for opening lanes and receives the opener's budget back |
| `KEEPER_LANES` · `KEEPER_DEMAND` | Engine: which lanes to keep open, and whether to open woken ones |
| `AI_MODEL` + `OPENAI_API_KEY` | Sensei and agents (or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY`, `AI_BASE_URL`) |
| `AGENT_XPUB` · `AGENT_XPRV` | Agent keys: the web derives vaults from the public key, the engine signs with the private one |
| `AUTH_SECRET` | Web: signs sign-in sessions |

</Step>
<Step>

### Run

```bash
pnpm --filter @joge/engine start
```

```bash
pnpm --filter @joge/web dev
```

Or build the two Dockerfiles (`apps/web/Dockerfile`, `services/engine/Dockerfile`) as the live deployment does.

</Step>
</Steps>

## Just a keeper

The contracts don't care who opens, locks, settles or pays. A keeper of your own with `ENGINE_COMPONENTS=oracle,indexer,keeper` and a funded `KEEPER_WIF` opens rounds on the lanes you choose and is paid the opener fee (0.5% of every pot of 200,000 sats or more) plus its budget back, by the same contracts. Two keepers sending the same step is harmless: the second one sees "already".

<Callout title="One keeper per key">
Two engines must never share a `KEEPER_WIF`: they would spend the same coins.
</Callout>
